name: Basilica of the National Shrine of Our Lady of Fatima
history: In 1954 a local landowner gave land to the Barnabite Fathers on the condition that a shrine to Mary be built. Polish and Italian Catholic communities around Niagara Falls took up the project. The church was begun in 1963, dedicated in 1965, and raised to a basilica in 1975.
arch: A Modernist church by architect Joseph E. Fronczak, crowned by a dome 100 feet across and covered in glass and acrylic glass shaped like the Northern Hemisphere.
features: A 13-foot Vermont granite statue of Our Lady of Fatima, weighing about 10 tons, stands on top of the dome.
A 48-foot bell tower was added in 1981 in memory of Father Charles M. Barlassina.

look.d: The 100-foot dome is drawn like the Northern Hemisphere, a globe you can walk under.
The statue on the dome is carved from Vermont granite and weighs about 10 tons.

fun: The Barnabites expected to build a simple grotto. The communities built this instead.
journal: A glass globe near Niagara Falls with Mary standing on top. Bold, and oddly gentle.

quiz.q: What is the statue on the dome made of?
